title: Shifted-sheaf detection of the scalar orientation equation
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E\subset S=\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sf-setting]. For $T=X,Y$, put $A_{n,T}=(R/\ell^n)_T$, $B_{n,T}=(S/\ell^n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site, and use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Write $\mathcal N_A(T),\mathcal N_B(T)$ for their normalized constructible subcategories with uniform cohomological and Tor bounds [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and $C_T=-\otimes^L_{A_{\bullet,T}}B_{\bullet,T}$ for scalar extension of whole systems [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Twists mean [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Write $P_A=Rf_{!,A,\bullet}\dashv G_A=f^!_{A,\bullet}$ and $P_B\dashv G_B$ for the specified tower adjunctions, with units $\eta_A,\eta_B$ and counits $\epsilon_A,\epsilon_B$ [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Fix the same compactification for the two compact-support functors [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Let $b:C_YP_A\xrightarrow{\sim}P_BC_X$ be the coefficient comparison formed by the proper direct-image coefficient mate followed by the open-extension tensor identification, as in [lem-sp-field-shriek-system-comparison]. Let $c_K:C_XG_AK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BC_YK$ be the $P_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $C_Y\epsilon_{A,K}\circ b_{G_AK}^{-1}$ [lem-sp-field-exceptional-system-comparison]. Put $J_{A,T}=(A_{n,T})_n$, $J_{B,T}=(B_{n,T})_n$, $\omega_A=G_AJ_{A,Y}$ and $\omega_B=G_BJ_{B,Y}$. Let $a_A:J_{A,X}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_A$ and $a_B:J_{B,X}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_B$ be the specified diagonal/DNC tower orientations of [det-sp-tower-gamma](1). Both dualizing systems have cohomology concentrated in degree $-2d$. Each orientation is the unique derived morphism induced by the compatible family of degree-$(-2d)$ finite orientation sheaf maps, after identifying a concentrated complex with its sole cohomology sheaf. Under $C_YJ_{A,Y}=J_{B,Y}$ and the canonical coefficient comparison of twists [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], one has the equality of actual tower morphisms
$$c_{J_{A,Y}}\circ C_X(a_A)=a_B.$$
The uniqueness assertion is restricted to these shifted degree-zero coefficient sheaves; equality of morphisms between them is componentwise equality of sheaf-system maps. No faithfulness of evaluations on arbitrary derived tower objects is asserted. The coefficient-unit finite orientations here have Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ before twisting, and the finite purity comparisons are those of [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3).

proof.text: Obtain normalized unit and line scalar comparisons and their finite evaluated orientation equations from the comparison-data lemma. Apply the one-field rigidity lemma separately to E and F. Use the canonical shifted-heart identification of the source line at F and compose it with the supplied orientation isomorphism to present the target as a shifted sheaf. Conjugate both candidate maps by these presentations, using fullness of the shifted single functor to recover sheaf maps. Exact evaluation commutes with single and shift; equality of all finite maps therefore implies equality of all sheaf components. Componentwise extensionality and faithfulness of single/shift prove equality of the actual maps. Cancel the line comparison to get the tower orientation square. Prove each finite unit has Tor amplitude [0,0] by transporting tensor with the unit to the identity via the existing smoothPurityUnitIso comparison and the tensor unitor; a degree-zero single sheaf has no other cohomology. Combine the remaining one-field conclusions.

proof_origin.note: Restore the quarantined complete proof after removing the stale scalarReductionSiteSmall attribute command. Prove single/shift naturality generically for exact functors and specialize to evaluation, avoiding tower coefficient expansion. Present the target by composing the source heart identification with the supplied orientation isomorphism; the mathematical route and proof dependencies are preserved.
